items.title: Arturo O'Farrill interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2024
items.q: the last cut on “The Offense of the Drum” is that arrangement of “Iko Iko” with Donald Harrison

ctx.x: That’s what I thought, and well your arrangement of it was quite inventive.

Todd Bashore arranged that piece. But I have to — you know it’s funny because that’s actually a piece that we recorded on a record that I love that I think is my breakthrough artistic moment. It’s a record that I made called “The Offense of the Drum” and the last cut on “The Offense of the Drum” is that arrangement of “Iko Iko” with Donald Harrison. And it’s really interesting to me because the thing about that arrangement and about that piece is that we talk a lot about Latin and jazz as being different or…

you know you look at this music and you realize that there’s two ways to hear music. You can hear a pulse orientation where you’re counting individual beats, or you can, and this is always the way to learn music by the way. But the grown-ups tend to see music as larger entities of phrase orientation, the larger entities, so that when, even playing jazz if you look — I have had this experience a thousand times in giving clinics where you have a saxophone section going [scats] and they’re playing [scats] and you…
